extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, assignees, and attorneys) preparing or examining reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and examiner guidance from the MPEP for preparing, filing, and examining patent reissue applications, including inventorship, drawings, and reissue oath/declaration content and timing. Covers distinctions for applications filed before/after September 16, 2012 and continuation/divisional reissue issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee may sign inventor’s oath/declaration (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application for the original patent was filed under 37 CFR 1.46 by the assignee of the entire interest, the assignee may sign the inventor’s oath or declaration; otherwise the signature of all inventors is needed except as provided in 37 CFR 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to reissue applications filed on or after September 16, 2012. If the assignee signs the reissue oath/declaration, and an inventor being deleted still has ownership interest, that inventor’s signature must also be included as an assignee. See MPEP § 324/325 and 37 CFR 1.46/1.64 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor consent/ownership when deleting an inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: If the name of an inventor is to be deleted and that inventor has not assigned rights to the patent (i.e., retains an ownership interest), the inventor must consent to the reissue (37 CFR 1.172(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the inventor being deleted consents and the remaining inventors sign the reissue oath/declaration, the deleted inventor need not sign. However, if an assignee signs the reissue oath/declaration, the inventor being deleted must be included in the oath/declaration as an assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures when adding an inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is being added in a reissue application, the inventor being added must sign the reissue oath or declaration together with the inventors previously designated on the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the added inventor refuses to sign, the assignee of the entire interest may sign a substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64. This applies even when the application both changes inventorship and enlarges claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-September 16, 2012 inventorship/signature rules (pre-AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications filed before September 16, 2012 that change the claims to enlarge scope, the signature of all inventors is needed; if an inventor refuses to sign because they dispute the inventorship change, filing may still be possible with a petition under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 together with written consent of all owners/assignees as required by pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.172(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the consent requirement cannot be met (e.g., no assignee and an inventor refuses to consent), a pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 petition will not be appropriate and resort to the courts may be required (35 U.S.C. 256).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean copy of drawings required at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit a clean copy (e.g., good quality photocopies free of any extraneous markings) of each drawing sheet of the printed patent at the time the reissue application is filed. If such copy complies with § 1.84, no further drawings will be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not transfer drawings from the patent file to the reissue application. New drawing sheets should not be submitted unless changes are made; changes must comply with 37 CFR 1.173(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheets required for amended drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to a patent drawing must be submitted as a replacement sheet of drawings attached to the amendment document; any replacement sheet must comply with § 1.84 and include all figures appearing on the original version of the sheet, even if only one figure is amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' added figures as 'New,' and canceled figures must be surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.' All changes must be explained in detail on a separate sheet accompanying the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical alteration of original/printed drawings prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Amending the original or printed patent drawing sheets by physically changing or altering them is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to physically change printed patent drawings should be denied; replacement sheets must be submitted instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated marked-up drawings permitted and labeled
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may include a marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, clearly labeled as 'Annotated Marked-up Drawings'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such marked-up copies must be presented in the amendment or remarks section that explains the change. The examiner may request a marked-up copy in an Office action; it must be provided when required by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notification if drawing changes not approved
rubrics_metrics.description: If any drawing change is not approved, or if any submitted sheet of drawings is not entered, the examiner will inform the reissue applicant in the next Office action and set forth the reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should clearly state the reasons for non-approval in the Office action so applicant can correct or respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and required filing of reissue oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration required by 37 CFR 1.175 must be filed with the application or within the time period set under 37 CFR 1.53(f) along with the required surcharge to avoid abandonment; the primary examiner must personally review and decide sufficiency of the reissue oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike non-reissue non-provisional applications, submission of the inventor’s oath/declaration in a reissue application cannot be delayed until payment of the issue fee—the oath/declaration must be executed before the case can be released for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration must state belief patent is inoperative or invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration must contain a statement that the applicant believes the original patent to be wholly or partly inoperative or invalid—(1) by reason of a defective specification or drawing, or (2) by reason of the patentee claiming more or less than patentee had the right to claim in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP provides example phrasings (e.g., 'Applicant believes the original patent to be partly inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective specification or drawing.'). If using PTO/SB/51 or PTO/SB/52 (or PTO/AIA/05/06), applicant must check appropriate box(es) identifying reasons; if not using a form, applicant must state each reason in the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration must identify at least one error (specificity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue applicant must acknowledge existence of an error in the specification, drawings, or claims which causes the original patent to be defective, and must specifically identify at least one such error being relied upon to support the reissue (35 U.S.C. 251).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one error need be specified; more than one may be specified; if some designated 'errors' are not errors under 35 U.S.C. 251, any remaining appropriate error still supports the reissue. It is not necessary to state how/when the error arose or was discovered; identification of 'at least one error' is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional specificity for broadening reissue (post-September 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application filed on or after September 16, 2012 that seeks to enlarge the scope of the claims, the reissue oath or declaration must identify a claim that the application seeks to broaden in the identification of the error relied upon to support the reissue; a general statement that all claims are broadened is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is sufficient to identify the claim being broadened and a single word, phrase, or expression in the specification or an original claim and how it renders the original patent wholly or partly inoperative or invalid. The corresponding corrective action need not be identified in the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient/impermissible error-statements (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic statements such as 'this application is being filed to correct errors in the patent which may be noted from the changes made in the disclosure' or merely reproducing claims with brackets/underlining without identifying specific errors are not sufficient; similarly, asserting 'failure to include a claim directed to …' by reciting new claim limitations without explaining what other claims lacked is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath/declaration must point to specific claim(s) and specific claim language or explain, at least generally, what the remaining claims contain relative to the canceled or added claims. Simply canceling 'unduly broad' claims without identifying what they lacked is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/divisional reissue oath reuse rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuing reissue application may satisfy the oath requirement by copying the oath/declaration from the parent reissue application only if certain conditions are met (e.g., the inventor executed the oath for the earlier-filed reissue, the continuing reissue does not seek to enlarge claims, or the original patent application was filed under § 1.46 by the assignee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the parent oath does not identify an error that supports the continuation/divisional, the examiner should reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 and require a new oath/declaration. For continuations/divisionals filed before Sep 16, 2012, petitions under 37 CFR 1.183 may be needed to waive pre-AIA requirements when relying on a parent oath for a different corrective action. See MPEP § 1414.01 and 37 CFR 1.175(f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration must comply with §§ 1.63, 1.64, 1.67 content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to identifying the error and belief, the reissue oath/declaration must include the statements required by 37 CFR 1.63 (and comply with 1.64 or 1.67 as applicable): that the signer believes the named inventor to be original inventor/joint inventor of a claimed invention, and that the application was made or authorized to be made by the person executing the oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person may not execute an oath/declaration unless they have reviewed and understand the contents of the application (including the claims) and are aware of the duty to disclose material information under 37 CFR 1.56. Depending on circumstances the oath/declaration may be prepared as PTO/AIA/05 (inventor), PTO/AIA/06 (assignee), or PTO/AIA/07 (substitute statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign and requirements for juristic entity or practitioner signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee of 100% of the entire right, title and interest (named as reissue applicant) may sign the declaration under certain conditions; if the reissue applicant is a juristic entity the declaration must be signed by an official with title carrying apparent authority or someone with a statement of authorization; a patent practitioner may sign for a juristic entity only if given authority (not merely power of attorney).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee/current owner may sign a substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 on behalf of an inventor who is deceased, incapacitated, cannot be found, or refuses to execute, even for broadening reissues. See MPEP § 325, § 604, and § 605.01 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA requirement: statement of no deceptive intention and supplemental oaths
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications filed before September 16, 2012 (pre-AIA), the reissue oath/declaration must state that all errors being corrected up to the time of filing arose without any deceptive intention on the part of the applicant, and any error corrected later must be accompanied by a supplemental oath/declaration stating no deceptive intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental oath/declaration must be submitted before allowance (with an amendment prior to allowance or to overcome a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 251). For corrections after allowance, supplemental oath/declaration must accompany the requested correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner form paragraphs and rejections for defective reissue oaths/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP provides specific form paragraphs (e.g., 14.01.01, 14.01.02, 14.01.03, 14.01.05, 14.01.06, and 14.14) for use when the reissue oath/declaration is defective (no statement of defect, no specific error identified, identified error not appropriate, multiple inappropriate errors, general defects, and rejection language under 35 U.S.C. 251).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes explain when to use each form paragraph and require that form paragraph 14.14 (rejection) follow the defect paragraph(s). If an oath/declaration identifies an error that is not an appropriate error under 35 U.S.C. 251, the examiner should indicate the oath is defective and use the appropriate form paragraph(s).
